title: In 1958, a Wave 1,720 Feet Tall Hit Alaska (Biggest Ever)

scenes.text: In 1958, a wave 1,720 feet tall hit Alaska.
That's taller than the Empire State Building. It's the biggest wave ever recorded.
A magnitude 7.8 earthquake dropped 40 million tons of rock into Lituya Bay. The water had nowhere to go but up.
It stripped every tree off the mountainside, down to bare rock, a third of a mile up.
Two people in a fishing boat rode over it. They lived to tell the story.
A wall of water 1,720 feet high. Alaska. 1958.

description:
In 1958 a wave 1,720 feet tall hit Lituya Bay, Alaska, the tallest wave ever recorded.
A magnitude 7.8 earthquake dropped about 40 million tons of rock into the bay, and the splash stripped the forest off the mountainside up to 1,720 feet. Five people died; a father and son in a small boat rode over the wave and survived.
Would you have survived in that boat? Comment below.
first_comment: The two survivors, a father and his seven-year-old son, were anchored in the bay and rode straight over the wave. Where would you rather be: in the boat, or on the shore?
